claims.text: Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can induce serrated phase boundaries in the lamellar colonies of eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Induced serrated phase boundaries will simultaneously improve room-temperature tensile strength and ductility relative to smooth lamellar interfaces.
Conventionally processed AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has dual-phase L12 and B2 lamellar colonies.
The conventional AlCoCrFeNi2.1 lamellar phase boundaries are smooth and straight.
Lamellar interfaces are prone to microcrack propagation and coalescence during tensile loading.
Smooth, straight phase boundaries facilitate early microcrack initiation.
Warm rolling followed by a short anneal can be tailored to generate serrated boundaries.
Interface serrations can be introduced without substantially changing phase fractions or lamellar spacing.
Serrated phase boundaries deflect cracks and increase the tortuosity of crack paths.
Increasing crack-path tortuosity delays microcrack initiation and inhibits microcrack coalescence.
Serrated interfaces act as local strain-hardening sites and augment back stresses across the lamellae.
Serrated interfaces enhance internal load partitioning and work hardening.
Enhanced load partitioning and work hardening allow higher stresses and greater uniform plastic deformation before failure.
Internal-stress accumulation and strain localization in FCC lamellae near phase boundaries drive rapid crack propagation and coalescence along lamellar interfaces.
The serrated-boundary material will have higher yield strength and ultimate tensile strength than the smooth-boundary baseline.
The serrated-boundary material will have higher room-temperature elongation at failure than the smooth-boundary baseline.
The proposed intervention is expected to be effective only for dual-phase lamellar eutectic HEAs whose interface morphology can be changed without disrupting phase fractions or lamellar spacing.
